claims.text: Spark plasma sintering can consolidate mixtures of RHEA powders and Cu.
Spark plasma sintering can provide large-scale reactive processing of RHEA–Cu composites.
Spark plasma sintering can produce a stable RHEA–Cu composite microstructure despite the components' positive heat of mixing.
A high positive heat of mixing between the refractory elements and Cu hinders uniform reaction and phase distribution.
Rapid, controlled SPS heating and applied pressure are suitable for processing the mixed powders.
Using an inert or reducing atmosphere during SPS helps minimize excessive diffusion and segregation.
The SPS temperature can be made high enough to induce solid-state reactions while remaining low enough to avoid Cu evaporation and excessive grain growth.
SPS forms finely dispersed interfacial reaction zones or intermetallic phases between the refractory and Cu phases.
The interfacial reaction zones or intermetallic phases act as bonding bridges that stabilize the composite architecture.
SPS provides ultrafast heating and significant Joule heating at particle contacts.
Localized Joule heating promotes rapid reaction kinetics while limiting diffusion distances.
Rapid consolidation reduces the time available for segregation driven by positive mixing enthalpy.
Reduced segregation time locks in a fine-scale, uniform microstructure.
The SPS-processed composite will have a more homogeneous phase distribution and finer microstructural features than a conventionally sintered composite.
The SPS-processed composite will have better mechanical integrity than a conventionally sintered composite.
The SPS-processed composite is likely to have greater irradiation resistance than a conventionally sintered composite.
Conventional sintering methods such as hot pressing tend to produce phase segregation or coarser microstructures because of slower heating and longer dwell times.
Excessive SPS temperature or dwell time can cause Cu segregation or undesired phase growth.
SPS performance may vary with composition, processing parameters, and scale-up.
